name: St. Anton am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: Cradle of alpine skiing. 305 km of slopes, legendary Après-Ski, and breathtaking summer hikes.
beschreibung:
Overview

St. Anton am Arlberg is situated at an elevation of 1,304 meters at the western terminus of the Stanzertal valley in the Landeck district, resting at the foot of the historic Arlberg Pass (1,793 m) on the border with Vorarlberg. Hemmed in by the jagged Lechtal Alps to the north and the glaciated Verwall mountains to the south, the village is home to approximately 2,400 residents. Universally celebrated as the Cradle of Alpine Skiing, St. Anton effortlessly marries legendary sporting heritage with cosmopolitan flair: a handsome pedestrianized village core lined with luxury hotels and fine dining contrasts with some of the most challenging off-piste terrain in the Alps. Providing direct access to Ski Arlberg—Austria's largest interconnected ski area—and superb summer hiking, St. Anton attracts alpine enthusiasts from across the globe.

History

Settled since medieval times, the valley was noted in 1275 as Vallis taberna. In 1386, Heinrich Findelkind founded the St. Christoph hospice on the treacherous pass to shelter travelers from blizzards. The village, originally called Stanz, was formally renamed St. Anton am Arlberg in 1927 after Saint Anthony of Padua. The town forged alpine history: on January 3, 1901, the Ski-Club Arlberg was founded at St. Christoph. Here, local visionary Hannes Schneider revolutionized ski technique, inventing the Arlberg stem-turn method and opening Austria's first ski school in 1920/21. Pioneering ski movies like The White Ecstasy (1931) spread the Arlberg legend worldwide, while the 1928 Arlberg-Kandahar race created modern competitive downhill skiing. The 1698 parish church was extended in 1932 by celebrated modernist architect Clemens Holzmeister. Ahead of the 2001 Alpine World Ski Championships, the railway was relocated, transforming the village center into today's park and promenade.

Getting there

St. Anton am Arlberg boasts exceptional transport links. By car, the S16 Arlberg expressway delivers motorists directly to the resort exit, while the scenic B197 Arlberg pass road offers summer access, supported by the 14-kilometer Arlberg Road Tunnel. By rail, St. Anton am Arlberg railway station is one of Europe's highest mountain stations serving scheduled international express trains, with direct ÖBB Railjets running every two hours between Vienna, Innsbruck, and Zurich, as well as seasonal ICE services from Germany. Complimentary village and ski buses operate every few minutes between the center, lift stations, and outer hamlets.

Tips

Ski Arlberg provides over 300 kilometers of groomed runs and more than 200 kilometers of deep-snow freeride descents, linked by modern marvels like the Galzigbahn funitel with its Ferris-wheel cabins and the Valluga cable car soaring to 2,811 meters (offering views across five countries). Visit the Museum St. Anton am Arlberg in the historic Villa Trier to explore the origins of alpine skiing. Unwind at the ARLBERG-well.com wellness center with heated indoor/outdoor pools and saunas. In spring, the iconic mass-start race The White Thrill draws thrill-seekers, while summer visitors can hike the Arlberg Trail or cycle into the serene Verwall Valley with its suspension bridge.
